items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: Warren Luening... and George Graham, who played lead trumpet with many big bands here. Both mentors of mine.

ctx.x: That’s right and you know I could do that for the next hour, just read them. So speaking of huge egos, do you find it necessary to have an ego in your business or is it better not to have one?

Well I mean if you’re a drummer, a trumpet player, or a rock guitarist, there’s a certain amount of confidence — you know when you’re playing by yourself, you’re playing a solo, there’s a certain amount of confidence we all need and I don’t think it should cross the line into ego but you need to have enough confidence in your own abilities I think. As the great George Graham, who was a great lead trumpet player, once told me there’s a fine line between getting discovered and found out. And so I think it’s the…
Can you explain that? Being discovered and found out?
